one_month_reasoning: Lam's September-quarter report falls inside the window. Aggregators estimate Oct 21-22; Lam had not posted a date by Sep 30 [20], but it reported on Oct 22 last year. The guide is $8.1B revenue and $2.15 EPS [1]. Contract memory prices are still rising in 4Q26 [4] and tool lead times of 12-24 months point to deep backlogs [9,10], so a beat and a solid December guide are likely. TSMC and ASML report in mid-October; TSMC is expected to frame 2027 capex at $75-90B [11,12], which should help. The offsets: the stock has already rallied about 20% from its Sep 16-17 closing low of $269, and DRAM and NAND spot prices cooled through September [5,6]. That cooling is a lead indicator the market watches for a memory top, and it could colour any capex commentary. The AI 'pacing' sentiment that caused the 18% drop in three days in September [19] also remains. I centre near spot (median about $326, a small tilt for the likely beat) with about 18% monthly volatility. That is about the stock's usual 18.6%, slightly wider than round 1 because realized volatility since the summer has been 55-73%.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 EPS $11.30 x 28x = $316, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (FY28 FCF/share about $10.45 at 3.2%, plus about $2/share net cash = $328, weight 0.4), giving about $321, roughly at spot. This rebases the P/E leg on FY28 consensus (~$11.7), less a small memory-spot haircut, and assumes a somewhat compressed late-cycle multiple in September 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $11.7 [2,17], less about 3.5%. The haircut is because September DRAM/NAND spot prices cooled (DDR4 -3.6%, NAND wafer -1%, slowing DDR5 inquiries) [5,6], an early sign that memory capex could slow during 2028. SEMI's +14% 2028 WFE [13] argues against a larger cut.

Today $324 is 27.6x FY28 consensus and about 34x FY27 [2]. Semicap usually de-rates toward the mid-20s as the market looks toward a peak [3]. But lead times of 12-24 months [9,10] give unusual backlog visibility into 2028, so I hold near today's forward multiple instead of the 26.5x supervisor reconciliation. At 28x, forward earnings growth has to justify it.

bear.story: Memory spot weakness spreads to contract prices in 1H27. The AI 'pacing' debate turns into hyperscaler capex restraint for 2028, and memory makers push out fab tools. CY27 WFE comes in near flat instead of SEMI's +22%, and the market prices a 2028 downturn: FY28 EPS about $8.5 at 23x.

base.story: CY27 WFE grows about 20-25% (SEMI ~$175B; sell-side higher) and TSMC capex reaches $75-90B. Lam outgrows WFE on etch/deposition intensity, and 12-24 month lead times keep backlog visible into 2028. FY28 EPS is about $11.5-12 at about 29x as growth decelerates.

bull.story: The supercycle extends: memory remains undersupplied into 2028, TSMC spends toward $90B, and SEMI's 2028 +14% proves conservative. FY28 EPS reaches $13+ at 37-38x.

thesis_break_reason: $210 is about 35% below spot and about 18.6x my FY28 EPS ($11.3), below both the July 29 capitulation close ($252) and the Sep 16-17 lows ($269). A close there most likely means the market is pricing an actual 2027-28 WFE decline: memory contract prices rolling over (following the spot softness), TSMC framing 2027 capex well below the ~$75B consensus, AI-capex restraint turning into order push-outs, or a major new China rule. That would not be ordinary 65%-volatility noise.

reasoning: Round 2 revisions follow the supervisor's findings. (1) I mislabeled $9.33 as FY28 consensus; it is FY27. FY28 consensus is about $11.7 [2,17], so my $10.50 was about 10% too low without cause. I rebase to $11.30: consensus less a 3.5% haircut for an in-lane signal the others lack, the cooling in DRAM/NAND spot prices through September [5,6], even as 4Q26 contract prices rise [4]. (2) I drop the Substack $48B TSMC-capex threshold; current sell-side views are $75-90B for 2027 [11,12]. (3) SEMI's July forecast (2027 +21.8%, 2028 +14.1%) replaces reliance on secondary broker WFE figures [13]. (4) New alternative data: equipment lead times for etch/deposition have doubled to about 12 months, with some tools at 24 months [9,10], and Lam postings are up about 79% y/y [8]. Both support backlog visibility into 2028. (5) Polymarket's pacing market is too thin to use, so it no longer shapes the bear case [18]. On the rebased EPS, 30x would give about $340. I choose 28x, near today's 27.6x forward, rather than 30x (late-cycle compression) or 26.5x (the supervisor's figure), because lead-time data argue against an early de-rating. Fair value is about $321, roughly spot, so this is not a big-edge call. Scenario-weighted mean is about $351; I use a lognormal-ish distribution with median about $335 and about 52% log volatility, and keep a slightly fat left tail for a memory-driven digestion scare. My fair value sits slightly above the supervisor's $310 because I keep a higher multiple; I agree with its EPS correction.
